newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale sets barley vote conditions, words.
newsitem.headline: Goodale sets barley vote conditions, words.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralhp Goodale on Friday set the conditions and specific questions for a farmers' vote on the Canadian Wheat Board's monopoly over barley trade, which will be held in the first quarter of 1997.
"All current prairie farmers who have grown barley at least once in the last five years will be eligible to vote," Goodale said in a statement.
The voting farmers will be asked to choose between the following two barley marketing options:
Remove all barley (both feed and malting/food) from the Canadian Wheat Board and place it entirely on the open market for all domestic and export sales.
Maintain the Canadian Wheat Board as the single-seller for all barley (both feed and malting/food), with the continuing exception of feed barley sold domestically.

Goodale's office said the voters would initially be based on CWB permit book data. But those who do not have a CWB permit book can establish their eligibility to vote by either producing documentary evidence that they have grown barley in the past five years or by swearing a legally binding affidavit to that effect.
The CWB held an 11 percent share of the world feed barley market in marketing year 1994/95 (August/July) and 48 percent of the world malting barley market, CWB figures showed.
Canada exported 30 percent of the feed barley it produced in that period, all through the CWB.
Half of Canada's barley is grown in Alberta, a province that held a plebiscite last November on whether the CWB should retain its export monopoly in feed and malt barley.
Some 66 percent of the more than 15,000 Alberta farmers who voted in the plebiscite favored optional marketing through the CWB.
There are about 110,000 CWB permit book holding farmers in western Canada.
